subject: POC connectivity & setup checklist — next steps and timeline
messages:
From: Aisha Roy <aisha.roy@medisprint.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: rahul.mehta@medisprint.com
Date: 2028-09-12T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: POC requirements & kickoff window

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move the evaluation forward and put together a short mutual action plan covering the POC environment. High level ask: we need a step-by-step for org setup, API key provisioning, IP allowlist guidance, and VPC peering requirements so our infra team can scope time.

Attached is a brief with our constraints (Medisprint-POC-requirements.pdf). Key constraints:
- We need the evaluation to run for 4 weeks starting 2028-10-02.
- Traffic will originate from our GCP project (gcp-med-01) and two static egress ranges (listed in the attachment).
- We prefer short-lived API keys for app testing but can accept a longer-lived service account if required for peering.

Can you send:
1) A checklist we can map to internal owners (network, security, app)
2) A canonical list of IPs/redwood endpoints to allow
3) Expected timeline for VPC peering (if needed) and proposed cutover date

Looping Rahul (infra@medisprint.com) who will own the network side.

Thanks,

Aisha Roy
Director, Platform Ops
MediSprint Health

<attachment: Medisprint-POC-requirements.pdf>

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Aisha Roy <aisha.roy@medisprint.com>
Cc: rahul.mehta@medisprint.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-13T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC requirements & kickoff window

Aisha —

Appreciate the detail. I sketched a compact onboarding checklist that aligns to your timeline and the typical MAP cadence. Attached is our one-page checklist (redwood-onboard-checklist.xlsx). High level items below so infra/security can triage:

1) Org & access
   - We will create a demo org for MediSprint in our control plane; please provide the canonical org name and the primary admin email (we suggest infra@medisprint.com).
   - We will invite 2 admin users and 3 viewers for the trial. Admins get API key issuance permissions.

2) API keys and auth model
   - For quick start: we can issue a scoped API key tied to the demo org (valid for the POC window).
   - If you prefer service-account-style access for peering, we provide service tokens and a short auth flow; let us know which you prefer.

3) Network allowlist (egress + endpoints)
   - Allow outbound to: api.redwood-inference.com on 443 (TLS).
   - IP ranges we use for hosted endpoints: 34.192.16.0/22, 54.201.0.0/18 (these are the ranges that will need to be allowed; we'll confirm finals at least 3 business days before cutover).

4) VPC peering
   - Peering is optional for lower-latency ingestion; if you want peering we require a small NAT/endpoint config on your side and a peering connection request from us. Typical lead time 5–7 business days from mutual signoff.

Proposed timeline:
 - 2028-09-18: finalize MAP & assign owners (this week)
 - 2028-09-21 to 2028-09-25: network and org setup (allowlist & invites)
 - 2028-09-28: smoke test with short-lived keys
 - 2028-10-02: POC start (4-week evaluation)

If that looks okay, I’ll open the HubSpot MAP and drop a draft timeline + owners (link below). Also happy to jump on 30-minute session with Rahul and your infra folks to walk through VPC peering specifics.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
https://redwood-inference.com

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: rahul.mehta@medisprint.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-14T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Network notes for peering & allowlist

Rahul / Aisha —

Quick technical notes from our infra team to help your network crew:

- If you do VPC peering: we only need a route to a single peered subnet and an advertised CIDR. Redwood's side will present a customer-facing endpoint inside our peered VPC and handle egress routing.
- If you cannot peer, the allowlist approach works; please ensure NAT IPs are stable for the session.

Minimal firewall rules we recommend to simplify troubleshooting:
- Outbound from your app nodes -> api.redwood-inference.com:443 (TLS)
- ICMP allowed between test nodes during smoke test (for latency/route verification)

Example AS-accept guidance:
- If you use Cloud NAT, list the static IPs in the attachment (medisprint-ip-list.csv) and we will validate connections.

Edge cases:
- Some enterprises block large TLS ciphers during pen tests; if your security team performs scanning please let us know and we’ll run compatibility checks.

I can be on the call to review route tables and peering proposals.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
